title: License Policy
description: A verbose description of how to handle artifact licenses.

allowed-licenses.title: Allowed Licenses
allowed-licenses.description: List of SPDX license expressions allowed outright.  Some artifacts may override this.

default-behavior.description: What to do for artifacts that do not fall into an allowed or forbidden license list.

unknown-license.description: What to do for artifacts that do not identify a license.

forbidden-licenses.title: Forbidden Licenses
forbidden-licenses.description: List of SPDX license expressions disallowed outright.  Some artifacts may override this.

aliases.title: License Aliases
aliases.description: SPDX license expression aliases.  Allows defining possible alternative names, for sources that don't follow SPDX identifiers.  Maps from the SPDX expression to the aliases.

urls.description: List of license URLs that file under this expression.

names.description: List of license names that file under this expression.

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.description: List of artifacts that override license or allowed/forbidden status.  The FIRST entry whose purl pattern matches is the one applied, so order matters: place a narrow rule such as 'pkg:npm/foo@2.*' above a broad 'pkg:npm/foo', or the broad one shadows it.

purl.title: Artifact pUrl Pattern
purl.description:
The artifact this rule covers, as a glob: '*' matches any run of characters and '?' matches exactly one.  A pattern naming no version covers every version of that artifact, and is anchored, so 'pkg:npm/special' does not reach 'pkg:npm/specialist'.

The version qualifier exists because packages change license mid-life, and forbidding the package outright would refuse the earlier versions that are still fine:

  pkg:npm/foo          every version
  pkg:npm/foo@2.*      the 2.x line only
  pkg:npm/foo@*-beta*  every pre-release
  pkg:maven/g/a@*?classifier=sources   one classifier, any version

Note that a glob is textual and cannot express 'version 7.11 and later'.  Covering a license change means listing the lines above it, and a new major release needs a new entry.

ref.title: Reference
ref.description: Reference or source for the explanation.

policy.description: License policy for this artifact.  Ignored when 'usage' is present, which is the more precise statement.

usage.title: Per-Usage Policy
usage.description:
A more precise allowance, keyed by the kind of dependency the artifact is used as, for example {"runtime": "forbid", "test": "allow"}.

A single 'allow' decides the whole map, however many 'forbid' entries sit beside it.  That is deliberate: this tool decides whether an artifact must exist in the target repository, not whether code may link against it.  An artifact cleared for test use has to be mirrored or the tests cannot run, so the entry above means 'mirror it'.  The full map is carried into the report, so the runtime prohibition is recorded rather than lost, and enforcing the split is the build's job.

Kinds are not uniform across ecosystems: 'test' and 'build' (a parent POM or an imported BOM) exist only for Maven, 'peer' only for npm, and PyPI publishes neither dev nor test dependencies.  An entry naming a kind the artifact's ecosystem does not have is simply never matched.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Analysis of the reason for this entry.

items.title: Reason
items.description: Analysis of the reason for this entry.

LicenseDeclaration.title: License Declaration
LicenseDeclaration.description: Declares the license under use.  This allows for a simple SPDX format string, or a dictionary to provide additional context.

uris.title: License URIs
uris.description: List of links to known license locations for the artifact.  People may include relative file locations for their personal records.  Any included references must be handled safely.

UsageDecision.title: Usage Decision
UsageDecision.description: Whether the artifact is permitted in this role.

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description: A comment, for users of the configuration.
